source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check BIOS ROM size
1. Get the latest BIOS firmware packet.
2. Zip the packet , and check if the  ROM Size if mapped the release note.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Check with release note , it should have record the BIOS fw size.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands:
# DUT: SMBIOS BIOS/ROM type-3 + dmesg ROM/flash size
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo dmidecode -t 3 2>&1 | grep -iE 'Size|ROM'; dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'ROM|flash' | grep -iE 'MB|KB' | head"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the BIOS/ROM size from SMBIOS + dmesg so the user confirms the flash ROM size is as expected.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; proposes SMBIOS type 3 and dmesg text, but type 3 is chassis information and neither source proves BIOS image size or physical flash capacity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; distinguishes archive, image payload and flash capacity and requires the exact packet/release note/board identity.
historical_reviews.workflow_logic: Historically labels the case YES with dmidecode type 3; that command is retained as history but is not technically applicable.
historical_reviews.round_02: YES; repeats the chassis/ROM grep without resolving measurement semantics.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms artifact semantics and board correlation are required and no firmware write is authorized.

original_test_intent: Verify the owner-approved BIOS firmware artifact's specified size against the vendor release note and, if separately required, distinguish that raw image size from package archive size and physical SPI flash capacity for the exact board/SKU.
original_method: Obtain the exact approved BIOS package and release note, preserve hashes, inspect archive members without executing or flashing them, measure the specifically identified artifact in the specified units and compare it with the release-note field; query physical flash capacity only through a separate validated read-only method if required.
manual_activity: The owner supplies the authoritative artifact, release note and measurement semantics and later issues the verdict. Hashing, safe archive inspection, byte measurement and comparison can be automated; no physical action or firmware write is required.
required_inputs: Exact board/SKU and intended BIOS version
Approved BIOS package, cryptographic hash and matching release note
Owner correction of whether 'Zip the packet' means compress, extract/unzip or inspect the archive
Definition of ROM Size: archive bytes, raw BIOS image bytes, declared image region or physical flash capacity
Release-note field, units, tolerance and any approved read-only flash inventory tool
safety_requirements: Do not flash, erase or write firmware; this case is artifact/inventory comparison only.
Inspect packages in an isolated non-system path and never execute bundled utilities or scripts during size extraction.
Do not use SMBIOS chassis type 3 or generic dmesg text as flash-capacity evidence.
Stop on package/SKU/hash mismatch, ambiguous member selection, units conflict or unexpected executable behavior; do not guess or auto-remediate.
agent_execution_scope: Validate board/package/release-note identity and hash and inventory archive contents safely.
Measure the owner-selected archive member/raw image and compare exact bytes plus converted units with the specified release-note field.
If separately approved, collect validated read-only flash-capacity evidence and report it in a distinct column; preserve Tool Result without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Resolve the source's zip/image/ROM-capacity ambiguity and approve the exact artifact/member and release-note field.
Provide any platform-approved physical flash inventory method if capacity is in scope.
Review the comparison and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: dmidecode -t 3 reports chassis data, not BIOS ROM capacity; dmesg ROM/flash strings are uncorrelated and neither compares the supplied package with its release note. The command is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use checksum and safe archive-list/extract metadata tools on the approved package, record exact member byte sizes and compare to the named release-note field. Use a vendor-approved read-only flash inventory tool only if physical capacity is explicitly required.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The literal 'latest', 'Zip the packet', ROM Size, release-note mapping and 5/0-minute fields are preserved; 'latest' must become an approved exact version before execution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a versioned manifest containing board/SKU, BIOS version, package/member hashes, archive/raw image byte sizes, declared regions and release-note field/units; report physical flash capacity separately.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact board/SKU and BIOS package declared in the manifest.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record package/release-note revision and artifact-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use the supplied BIOS release note and platform firmware packaging/flash documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Prevents compressed-size/raw-image/capacity conflation and replaces irrelevant host greps with exact artifact measurements.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; every size concept requested by the owner is retained as a separate metric.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner semantic correction, exact package/member and release-note field.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Compressed archive size varies by compression and metadata and cannot prove raw ROM image or flash capacity.

project_override_considerations: A project supplies the exact BIOS package and selects the size metric(s). Missing artifacts are readiness gates, not PARTIAL/BLOCKED; the master source ambiguity remains documented and is not overwritten by a project convention.
expected_evidence: Board/SKU, exact BIOS version, package/release-note identifiers and hashes
Owner decision for zip/extract and archive/image/capacity semantics
Safe archive listing, selected member path/hash and exact byte/unit measurements
Release-note comparison table, any separate validated flash-capacity evidence, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item says ROM Size, step 2 says to 'Zip the packet,' and the criterion refers to BIOS firmware size in the release note. Compressed archive size, raw image size and physical ROM capacity are non-equivalent; the owner must identify which value the source intends without silently rewriting it.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Although measurement semantics require owner correction, the artifact-comparison purpose and safe execution path are clear. Once the selected metric and files are supplied, the full core is automatable; this is not permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its technically irrelevant chassis/dmesg command while retaining the concept of electronic evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its size distinctions and artifact safeguards but reclassifies PARTIAL to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because package/semantic inputs do not create a manual core.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Elevates the non-equivalent size terms to an explicit SOURCE_CONFLICT and defines separate auditable metrics.

review_improvement: Prevents a false ROM-size conclusion from chassis data or compressed bytes, avoids firmware writes and keeps a fully electronic comparison correctly classified.
independent_technical_reasoning: The technical work is safe static artifact inspection and optional read-only capacity inventory, all automatable. Owner selection of the intended metric is a readiness/source-resolution input, not a reason to label the capability partial or permanently blocked.
